column8: Fri 20 Nov: 3a, one clause with row 3, the card's best: Kelly's own exception (refilled from outside every week, chase the average) read at source, p. 926; Q123-005 used the same paragraph for bet size and is merged, so this row carries it; never as Kelly backing the ladder, since Kelly's rule on J.P. Morgan's figures sizes shares far above the plan (Q123-020, Q123-040); one outside name per part.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q199-001: Peters and Gell-Mann's two conditions restate Kelly's refill (wealth that adds up) and row 7's pooling; the physicist's version adds a source, not a point.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a or 3f with row 1: the case's clause (no adding or withdrawing before 2033, l.63-65; no outside money for the payments, l.91-92) switches off Kelly's refill, so every miss was settled on 1 Jan 2033 and never made up (NUMBERS 8s); fix the wording: never this clause, not Laura's temperament, as a rival to IPS l.9's reason (CANON A3: the first plan was dropped for how a writer is paid); say the clause takes the refill away and IPS l.9 says her career, the one refill she has, shrinks in the same recession.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q199-010: stake size against wealth is Caius's point, read at source; Huygens himself not read; $302,287 is NUMBERS 1 and two-thirds of the two deposits is Keel arithmetic.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 or 3a, one clause: Bernoulli's figures reproduce (6,751, 7,033, cap 7,200 = 0.9 x 8,000); spreading collects the average only when ships sink one by one, while shares, her advances and co-sponsors' budgets can fall in the same downturn (IPS l.9; can, never fall together, card Q50); the limit is Keel's reading of his independence assumption, never that Bernoulli named it; competes for 2.3's one outside name with Bodie, Merton and Samuelson.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q199-005: the same section 16 rule in words; row 5 carries its worked figures.

Fri 20 Nov: store, beside row 9: pooling delivers the average only for separate coins; fix: co-sponsors can cut budgets in the same downturn (card Q50), never cut in it as a rule; the case already bars their money from the payments (l.91-92), so this explains and decides nothing.

Fri 20 Nov: 3f context or a judge's question only: all 25 failing US windows since 1871 start Oct 1927 to Oct 1929, one episode, not 25 chances (NUMBERS 8s says so); history is context, never a replacement for the 27 Sep figures; US stocks, not world shares, rates fixed.

Fri 20 Nov: wording guard for 3a and 3f: the simulated average is across possible histories, not across investors, since everyone holding shares lives the same market; corrects store H5-002's an average across many investors; say the average across simulated futures (WORDS); Keel inference on sources read, so S 3.

Fri 20 Nov: store or 3a pedigree: Caius should pay 1.6 times the expected loss if poor (5,043 reproduces); fix: the ten are about two-thirds of the two deposits, never of Laura's money, since her wealth outside the portfolio is not in the case (l.61-63), so Bernoulli's test cannot be run on her; never insurance, CPPI or portfolio insurance for the plan.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q199-012: Bernoulli's poor fellow is the worked case of price against worth; a classic, and close to Savage's ticket-holder (Q182-001).

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3's career line or References, pedigree for IPS l.9: VT costs Laura what it costs anyone and is worth less to her as payment money because it falls when her advances do; Bernoulli's circumstance is wealth, not an income tied to markets, so one clause, never as Bernoulli's own point.

Fri 20 Nov: CONCEIT candidate for 3a, one turn at most, never a second conceit or in tables; fix (this morning's blind judges): five of the ten and both ends of the range rest on iBond funds that pay net asset value and seek no predetermined amount, so never a fund's payout as cargo already landed: say a Treasury or a fund of Treasuries ending that year; each rung reaches $50,000 only with its interest reinvested and the extra Treasuries behind it (NUMBERS 1, 2).

Fri 20 Nov: Table 2's note or 3e, a clause at most: J.P. Morgan's row prints the average year (8.94%) beside the compound 7.50%, and the plan uses the compound, the median future's rate (NUMBERS 0: VT median growth); the lognormal check reproduces (0.0133); pedigree only; the 7.5% is above the middle of published forecasts, no median figure (CANON B15).

Fri 20 Nov: 3f, spine row 10's price said two ways: $35,305 less on average, about $19,000 less at the median, more in 44 markets in 100 (NUMBERS 8s, Keel arithmetic, MODEL); fixes: say at the median, never in the middle future, for a difference of two medians; never name ergodicity in 3f (no outside names, panel 4); the 1.88 ratio is Keel arithmetic, never a plan figure; never $19,000 alone, with today's engine's $65,000 for the plan as built.

Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q37-018 (at 4% to 10% the stated top is $115,000 in every column): the 9% column ($117,972 against $117,142, NUMBERS 4) adds only the Peters framing; the top before the move rests on the 7.5% forecast, so model, never a plan figure.

Fri 20 Nov: store: over three years the spread of VT's outcome is about seven times the gap between average and median (Keel arithmetic on CANON B15, lognormal assumed, S 3 at most); supports that which average is used barely matters; never a plan figure; Q6-025 holds the band itself.

Fri 20 Nov: 3f defence for a judge's question or the store: the 27 Sep model solved its lognormal so compound (6.70%) and arithmetic (7.94%) both match (NUMBERS 8s inputs), so 1 in 31 is no artefact of using the average year; not prose in 3f (no outside names).

Fri 20 Nov: guard for 3f: corrects card Q168 idea 2(b) and Q168-011's use: 1 in 31 was, if the 27 Sep model was right, Laura's own chance, never a promise about copies of her; one-time decisions need no ensemble (Doctor, Wakker and Wang, supplementary information read at source).

Fri 20 Nov: store or References, with row 19: the critics' own objection (dated consumption, outcomes with no growth rate) fits ten dated payments and her credibility (case l.114-115); the liability-matching reading is Keel's, not theirs; needs the quarrel set up, so one clause at most, one outside name per part.
Fri 20 Nov: store: a single score can rank absurdly when a rare disaster is in play; built to be extreme, it says nothing about VT; no part needs it.

Fri 20 Nov: store: Peters and Gell-Mann concede one-shot bets fall outside their method; Laura's 2031 statement is near one-shot and the plan states the top only after the move buys it; 3c's one outside name is Neyman, so References at most.

Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q168-019 (the move as the day the average becomes her path; a top named 12 months early exceeds what the move buys in 10.6%, NUMBERS 4): adds only the absorbing-boundary quote; the why is the case's own (l.114-115) and spine row 7 carries it; wording right: the move would buy less than the stated top, never not yet owned.

Fri 20 Nov: store: the plan chooses which money is exposed to compounding; fix (this morning's blind judges): five of the ten rest on iBond funds that pay net asset value and seek no predetermined amount, so never a fixed sum on a fixed day for them; each rung's interest is reinvested at rates not yet known and met by the escrow standard (NUMBERS 2), so never promised dollars leave the compounding world.

Fri 20 Nov: merged into H3-031 (Samuelson's fallacy of large numbers), with H3-030: the textbook common error is the same family; the 35.6% of misses with no year down 20% is NUMBERS 8s; never say the IPS rejected time diversification (CANON A3).

Fri 20 Nov: 3f's frame in the team's own words (what her income does, not how brave she is), Peters in References only (3f names no outside source, panel 4); IPS l.9's reason told, never its sentence repeated (CANON A3); her taste for risk kept in the half promised to no one (IPS l.15).
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q199-028: Meder et al. read only through Peters (18 people; the critics' ambiguity reading, row 29); row 28 carries the later tests, one read at source.

Fri 20 Nov: store: circumstance moves caution and temperament persists (2022 read at source; 2024 a preprint by Peters's own group, abstract only, not independent); a clause for idea 5 at most, never proof that ergodicity replaced expected utility.
Fri 20 Nov: guard for any use of Peters: claim only what both sides grant (circumstances change caution); ambiguity aversion explains the experiment too; never ergodicity replaced expected utility.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q199-029: the unsettled exchange (opening lines only, paywalled) is the same guard; a better source than Q168-020's university summary for the comment's tone.
Fri 20 Nov: store, trivia: Whitworth's 1870 promise that a fair wager hurts both parties; the appendix was not read, so the argument is unverified; serves no part.
